# Windows dotfiles — chezmoi config template.
# Rendered once at `chezmoi init`; answers are stored in
# %USERPROFILE%\.config\chezmoi\chezmoi.toml and never re-asked.
#
# This repo targets **native Windows + PowerShell 7 (pwsh)** only. There is no
# OS branching: everything here assumes Windows. WSL/macOS/Linux are handled by
# the separate cross-platform dotfiles repo.

[data]
    # role picks coarse defaults; every toggle can still be overridden.
    role  = "workstation"
    name  = "hanruzhou"
    email = "hanruzhou+odspmdb@microsoft.com"

    # --- feature toggles (role-defaulted) ---
    installCodingAgents  = true
    # How a coding agent announces it finished. Gates HOOK WIRING ONLY — the
    # peon CLI installs alongside the agents so you can experiment any time.
    #   none   = silent
    #   notify = notify.ps1 -> apprise -> Windows toast (current behavior)
    #   peon   = peon-ping game voice lines + its own overlay banner
    #   both   = toast + voice (two banners; `peon notifications off` to trim)
    # peon's own volume/pack/notification style stay unmanaged by chezmoi, so
    # tweaking them never shows up as drift. Parent repo: docs/tools/agent-sounds.md
    agentSounds          = "notify"
    installSpecstoryBuild = true
    installWindowsApps   = true
    installWsl           = true
    installWslUbuntu     = false
    wslUsername          = "fareast\\hanruzhou"
    wslUbuntuBootstrap   = "headless"
    installUtilityApps   = true
    installGamingApps    = false
    installExtraRuntimes = true
    installMediaTools    = false
    installLlmTools      = true
    installTunnelTools   = false
    installIacTools      = false
    installSshServer     = false
    installHerdr         = true
    installClink         = true
    installTry           = true
    # translate has no scoop/winget manifest and no prebuilt Windows release, so
    # it is built from source with `go install` (go is pulled in by the block
    # itself). First apply on a fresh box therefore spends a few minutes here.
    installTranslate     = true
    # Rime input method (Weasel / 小狼毫). Same key name as the parent repo's
    # installInputMethod (Squirrel on macOS, ibus-rime on Linux) so the shared
    # Rime YAML in .chezmoitemplates/rime/ is gated identically on both sides.
    # winget's manifest is machine-scope NSIS, so applying prompts for UAC; and
    # its silent path registers SIMPLIFIED Chinese unless the installer also
    # gets /T (see Install-Weasel in the packages script).
    installInputMethod   = false
    useChineseMirror     = false
    managedMachine       = true
    backupMode           = "smart"
    enableVimMode        = true

# Run .ps1 scripts (.chezmoiscripts + modify_/create_) under PowerShell 7.
[interpreters.ps1]
    command = "pwsh"
    args = ["-NoProfile", "-NonInteractive"]

[diff]
    exclude = ["scripts"]

[status]
    exclude = ["scripts"]

```

---
name: dotfiles-windows
description: Operate and navigate THIS Windows machine's chezmoi-managed dotfiles (native PowerShell 7). Use when the user asks how to apply/edit/diff dotfiles, where a config or tool lives, how the pwsh $PROFILE / copilot-proxy / scoop+winget install works, how a keybinding or helper (applaunch/sysvol/x/cas) works, or how to use chezmoi / just in this repo.

# dotfiles-windows

This machine's `$HOME` is managed by a **chezmoi** dotfiles repo targeting **native
Windows + PowerShell 7**. Packages install via **scoop** (CLI) + **winget** (GUI) —
there is no ansible here. Repo: <https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles-windows>.
(macOS/Linux/WSL are handled by the separate `daviddwlee84/dotfiles` repo.)

## Orientation
- Source dir: `chezmoi source-path` — edit there (`cd "$(chezmoi source-path)"`).
- Preview / apply: `chezmoi diff` / `chezmoi apply` (or `just diff` / `just apply`).
- Source of a target: `chezmoi source-path <path>`; render without applying: `chezmoi cat <path>`.
- Re-run init prompts: `chezmoi init` (answers persist in `~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml`).
- `docs/**`, `editors/**`, `scripts/**` are chezmoi-ignored (not deployed).

## Shell layout (pwsh)
- `$PROFILE` (`~/Documents/PowerShell/Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1`) is a loader
  that dot-sources `~/.config/powershell/profile.d/*.ps1` in sorted order, then
  `~/.config/powershell/local.ps1` (untracked user override, loaded last).
- Fragments: `00_env` (PATH/XDG/env), `10_tools` (starship, zoxide, atuin,
  fzf, direnv, tv), `20_aliases` (`ll`/`gs`/`reload`/`cas`/`cau`/`chezmoi-cd`/`run-for`),
  `25_herdr` (`hvibe`/`hcode`/`hhere`/`hroot`/`hmark` workspace helpers, gated on herdr),
  `30_apps` (`applaunch`/`appquit`/`apprestart`/`sysvol`/`sysmute`/`x`), `35_yazi` (`y`),
  `40_copilot` (imports the Copilot module), `90_psreadline` (vi-mode gated on `enableVimMode`).

# Package-source policy shared by apply-time installers and interactive pwsh.
# Precedence is intentional: a managed/corporate machine must stay on the
# company-approved pull-through registries even if useChineseMirror was also
# selected. NuGet is provisioned machine-wide by IT; Go/Cargo keep their normal
# defaults because no company endpoints were discovered for them.
{{ if .managedMachine -}}
$env:PIP_INDEX_URL       = 'https://packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io/pypi/simple/'
$env:UV_DEFAULT_INDEX    = 'https://packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io/pypi/simple/'
$env:npm_config_registry = 'https://packagefeedproxy.microsoft.io/npm/'
{{ else if .useChineseMirror -}}
$env:PIP_INDEX_URL        = 'https://pypi.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/simple'
$env:UV_DEFAULT_INDEX     = 'https://pypi.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/simple'
$env:npm_config_registry  = 'https://registry.npmmirror.com'

import os
import sys

tmpl_path = os.environ["HERDR_TEMPLATE_FILE"]
live_path = os.environ["HERDR_LIVE_FILE"]
out_path = os.environ["HERDR_OUT_FILE"]

with open(tmpl_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    template_text = fh.read()


def emit(text):
    with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fh:
        fh.write(text)


try:
    import tomllib  # Python 3.11+
except ModuleNotFoundError:
    try:
        import tomli as tomllib
    except ModuleNotFoundError:
        # No TOML reader -> can't safely merge; ship the managed template as-is.
        emit(template_text)
        sys.exit(0)

try:
    import tomlkit
except ModuleNotFoundError:
    print(
        "modify_config.toml: tomlkit unavailable; emitting managed template "
        "(runtime keys not preserved this run)",
        file=sys.stderr,
    )
    emit(template_text)
    sys.exit(0)

# Tables the template owns outright.
MANAGED = {"theme", "ui", "terminal", "keys"}
# Single keys re-asserted into an otherwise pulled-through table.
FORCED = {("update", "channel"): "preview"}

with open(live_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    live_text = fh.read().strip()

doc = tomlkit.parse(template_text)  # base, with comments intact
try:
    live = tomllib.loads(live_text) if live_text else {}
except tomllib.TOMLDecodeError:
    # A corrupt live file must not block the apply — enforce the template.
    print("modify_config.toml: live config is not valid TOML; enforcing template", file=sys.stderr)
    live = {}

for key, value in live.items():
    if key in MANAGED:
        continue
    if key in doc:
        # The template also declares this table. Keep herdr's runtime keys and
        # let the template win only on the keys it actually sets.
        if isinstance(value, dict) and isinstance(doc[key], dict):
            for sub_key, sub_value in value.items():
                if sub_key not in doc[key]:
                    doc[key][sub_key] = sub_value
        continue
    doc[key] = value

for (table, sub_key), forced_value in FORCED.items():
    if table not in doc:
        doc[table] = tomlkit.table()
    doc[table][sub_key] = forced_value

emit(tomlkit.dumps(doc))

#!/usr/bin/env pwsh
# chezmoi modify_ script: overlay a managed herdr config onto ~/.config/herdr/config.toml.
#
# Runs under pwsh via [interpreters.ps1] in .chezmoi.toml.tmpl. chezmoi pipes the
# CURRENT target file into stdin and takes the new contents from stdout.
#
# WHY AN OVERLAY (this replaced a plain managed dot_config/herdr/config.toml):
# herdr rewrites this file at runtime — the onboarding flag, in-app settings
# popups, [session] / [remote] / [experimental] / [update] state. A plain managed
# file clobbers all of that on every `chezmoi apply`, which can re-trigger
# onboarding. The parent (unix) repo hit this and moved create_ -> modify_ on
# 2026-07-06; this repo's config was added five days later and still used the
# plain form. Same fix, ported.
#
# MERGE MODEL — template-as-base, pull-through unmanaged keys:
#   - Base = the managed template (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml), which
#     carries the comments + the tmux-parity rationale.
#   - Every TOP-LEVEL key in the live file that is NOT managed and NOT already in
#     the template is copied across (preserves onboarding, [session], [remote],
#     [experimental], and any future herdr writeback).
#   - Managed tables are enforced wholesale (template wins).
#   - FORCED single keys are re-asserted INTO a pulled-through table, so the table
#     keeps herdr's own bookkeeping. Windows needs exactly one: update.channel
#     must stay "preview" (the installer rejects "stable" on Windows builds), but
#     [update] also holds herdr's last-check state, which we do not want to wipe.
#     This sub-key merge is the one deliberate divergence from the unix overlay.
#
# WHY tomlkit (not a hand-rolled emitter): herdr's config has an array-of-tables
# ([[keys.command]]) and comments worth keeping; stdlib tomllib is read-only.
# Python runtime: prefer `uv` (guarantees >=3.11 -> stdlib tomllib), fall back to
# system python, then to emitting the raw template (a fresh host with neither
# still gets a full config — note we emit the TEMPLATE, not stdin, because on a
# fresh host stdin is empty).
#
# To manage an additional key: edit .chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml.
# Validate the result with `herdr server reload-config` (empty diagnostics).

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

# modify_ scripts run under `pwsh -NoProfile`, so the deployed 05_mirrors.ps1
# fragment is not loaded here. Apply the same source policy inline before uv
# resolves tomlkit: managed machines must use the IT-approved pull-through feed.
{{ template "package-sources.ps1" . }}

# Emit bytes verbatim so nothing re-encodes the config's ⭐ / box-drawing glyphs
# and no BOM or trailing CRLF churn creeps into chezmoi's diff.
function Write-StdoutBytes {
    param([byte[]] $Bytes)
    $out = [Console]::OpenStandardOutput()
    $out.Write($Bytes, 0, $Bytes.Length)
    $out.Flush()
}

$utf8 = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)   # no BOM

$templateText = @'
{{ template "herdr/config.toml" . }}
'@

$liveText = [Console]::In.ReadToEnd()

$tmpDir = [System.IO.Path]::GetTempPath()
$stamp = [System.IO.Path]::GetRandomFileName()
$tmplFile = Join-Path $tmpDir "herdr-tmpl-$stamp.toml"
$liveFile = Join-Path $tmpDir "herdr-live-$stamp.toml"
$pyFile = Join-Path $tmpDir "herdr-merge-$stamp.py"
$outFile = Join-Path $tmpDir "herdr-out-$stamp.toml"

try {
    [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($tmplFile, $templateText, $utf8)
    [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($liveFile, $liveText, $utf8)

    # Pick a Python. uv is in this repo's scoop package set; `python` is the
    # uv-managed default install (--default --preview creates the unversioned shim).
    $py = $null
    if (Get-Command uv -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
        $py = @('uv', 'run', '--no-project', '--quiet', '--with', 'tomlkit', '--python', '>=3.11', 'python')
    } elseif (Get-Command python -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
        $py = @('python')
    } elseif (Get-Command python3 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
        $py = @('python3')
    }

    if (-not $py) {
        [Console]::Error.WriteLine('modify_config.toml: no uv/python found; emitting managed template (runtime keys not preserved this run)')
        Write-StdoutBytes $utf8.GetBytes($templateText)
        return
    }

    $pySource = @'
import os
import sys

tmpl_path = os.environ["HERDR_TEMPLATE_FILE"]
live_path = os.environ["HERDR_LIVE_FILE"]
out_path = os.environ["HERDR_OUT_FILE"]

with open(tmpl_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    template_text = fh.read()


def emit(text):
    with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fh:
        fh.write(text)


try:
    import tomllib  # Python 3.11+
except ModuleNotFoundError:
    try:
        import tomli as tomllib
    except ModuleNotFoundError:
        # No TOML reader -> can't safely merge; ship the managed template as-is.
        emit(template_text)
        sys.exit(0)

try:
    import tomlkit
except ModuleNotFoundError:
    print(
        "modify_config.toml: tomlkit unavailable; emitting managed template "
        "(runtime keys not preserved this run)",
        file=sys.stderr,
    )
    emit(template_text)
    sys.exit(0)

# Tables the template owns outright.
MANAGED = {"theme", "ui", "terminal", "keys"}
# Single keys re-asserted into an otherwise pulled-through table.
FORCED = {("update", "channel"): "preview"}

with open(live_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    live_text = fh.read().strip()

doc = tomlkit.parse(template_text)  # base, with comments intact
try:
    live = tomllib.loads(live_text) if live_text else {}
except tomllib.TOMLDecodeError:
    # A corrupt live file must not block the apply — enforce the template.
    print("modify_config.toml: live config is not valid TOML; enforcing template", file=sys.stderr)
    live = {}

for key, value in live.items():
    if key in MANAGED:
        continue
    if key in doc:
        # The template also declares this table. Keep herdr's runtime keys and
        # let the template win only on the keys it actually sets.
        if isinstance(value, dict) and isinstance(doc[key], dict):
            for sub_key, sub_value in value.items():
                if sub_key not in doc[key]:
                    doc[key][sub_key] = sub_value
        continue
    doc[key] = value

for (table, sub_key), forced_value in FORCED.items():
    if table not in doc:
        doc[table] = tomlkit.table()
    doc[table][sub_key] = forced_value

emit(tomlkit.dumps(doc))
'@

    [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($pyFile, $pySource, $utf8)

    $env:HERDR_TEMPLATE_FILE = $tmplFile
    $env:HERDR_LIVE_FILE = $liveFile
    $env:HERDR_OUT_FILE = $outFile

    $exe = $py[0]
    $rest = @($py[1..($py.Count - 1)]) + @($pyFile)
    & $exe @rest
    $rc = $LASTEXITCODE

    if ($rc -ne 0 -or -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $outFile)) {
        [Console]::Error.WriteLine("modify_config.toml: merge failed (exit $rc); emitting managed template")
        Write-StdoutBytes $utf8.GetBytes($templateText)
        return
    }

    Write-StdoutBytes ([System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($outFile))
} finally {
    foreach ($f in $tmplFile, $liveFile, $pyFile, $outFile) {
        Remove-Item -LiteralPath $f -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    }
    foreach ($v in 'HERDR_TEMPLATE_FILE', 'HERDR_LIVE_FILE', 'HERDR_OUT_FILE') {
        Remove-Item "env:$v" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    }
}

```

# --- npm CLI agents --------------------------------------------------------
function Npm-InstallGlobal([string[]]$pkgs) {
    if (-not (Have npm)) { foreach ($p in $pkgs) { Register-Failure "npm:$p (npm unavailable)" }; return }
    foreach ($p in $pkgs) {
        Info "npm i -g $p"
        npm install -g $p 2>&1 | Out-Host
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Register-Failure "npm:$p" }
    }
}

# --- herdr (native Windows terminal multiplexer, preview beta) --------------
# No scoop/winget/npm manifest — installs via herdr.dev's irm|iex bootstrap
# (same shape as Ensure-Scoop). Windows builds are preview-only; the bin junction
# is %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Herdr\bin (added to PATH in profile.d/00_env.ps1).
function Install-Herdr {
    $herdrBin = Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA 'Programs\Herdr\bin\herdr.exe'
    if ((Have herdr) -or (Test-Path -LiteralPath $herdrBin)) { Info 'herdr already installed'; return }
    Info 'installing herdr (preview) via herdr.dev/install.ps1'
    try {
        $env:HERDR_CHANNEL = 'preview'   # Windows builds are preview-only
        $installer = [scriptblock]::Create((Invoke-RestMethod https://herdr.dev/install.ps1))
        & $installer
        if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $herdrBin)) { Register-Failure 'herdr' }
    } catch {
        Write-Warning "herdr install error: $_"
        Register-Failure 'herdr'
    }
}

`installHerdr = true` enables the installation attempt; it does not guarantee success.

What happened:

1. The package script entered the enabled Herdr block in `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1.tmpl#L535-L538`.
2. The official installer downloaded and verified Herdr.
3. After executing the staged binary for verification, Defender or Windows Search temporarily held it open.
4. The installer then failed while renaming the staging directory into the active release directory with “Access denied.”
5. The package script deliberately records individual failures and continues, so `chezmoi apply` itself does not fail.
6. Because this is a `run_onchange` script, another unchanged apply does not necessarily rerun it. The earlier “re-run apply” advice is misleading for this case.

This was **not** an IT policy rejection like Tailscale, and no security controls were disabled.

The verified staged release has now been safely activated through the official installer:

- Herdr version: `0.8.0-preview.2026-08-04-d78e3d3b5126`
- Official managed junction and user `PATH` entry created
- Open a new PowerShell window for `herdr` to resolve normally.

name: agent-history-hygiene

Use when the user says "commit my chat", "save this specstory session", "stage the plan file", "scrub the transcript", "my .env leaked in chat", "bootstrap pre-commit for this project", or when you notice untracked `.specstory/history/*.md` or `.claude/plans/*.md` files while running `git status`. Also use after an accidental push of a secret to enforce rotate-first, rewrite-last remediation instead of reflexive `git push --force`.
---

# agent-history-hygiene

Keep agent chat transcripts and plan files committed together with the
code they produced, without leaking secrets. Pairs with the
`redact-agent-secrets` + `gitleaks` pre-commit hooks the skill installs.

Three surfaces, separated by purpose:

| Surface                          | Question it answers                                          |
|----------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| `find-session.sh`                | "Which transcript / plan file is *my* current session?"      |
| `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`       | "Which agent files belong in the next commit?"               |
| `bootstrap-project.sh`           | "How do I get pre-commit + gitleaks + redactor into a repo?" |
| `scan-staged.sh`                 | "Is there a leaked secret in what I'm about to commit?"      |
| `references/remediation.md`      | "I already pushed a secret — now what?"                      |

  script's shebang (`#!/bin/sh`) + exec bit; Windows honors neither, so it can't
  run the script reliably — and you can't hand it a `.ps1` extension, because
  that's fixed to the target name. Only `[interpreters.ps1] = pwsh` is wired up,
  and it only helps when the *managed file itself* is a `.ps1`.
- **Wrong toolchain.** The parent filter is `sh` + `jq` — not guaranteed on a
  pwsh-first box, and rewriting it in pwsh still hits the routing wall above.

So each merge is a **`run_onchange_after_*.ps1.tmpl`** in `.chezmoiscripts/`
instead: a real `.ps1` that routes cleanly through `[interpreters.ps1] = pwsh`,
runs natively with no external deps, and recursively deep-merges a
chezmoi-ignored overlay (`editors/*.json`, `claude/settings-overlay.json`,
embedded via `{{ include }}`) into the live file — preserving every key the tool
wrote. This is invariant #5 in `AGENTS.md`.

**Tradeoff:** a `modify_` filter re-asserts on *every* apply; `run_onchange` only
re-fires when its rendered content (the overlay) changes. If the tool later
overwrites a managed key, it isn't restored until the overlay changes or you
reset state (`chezmoi state delete-bucket --bucket=entryState`). The parent needs
every-apply enforcement because CodeIsland / workmux keep rewriting
`~/.claude/settings.json`; Windows has no such contenders, so the lighter trigger
is fine.

## XDG paths, not `%APPDATA%`

Windows and XDG split directories on different axes — Windows by whether a
folder *roams* (`AppData\Roaming` vs `AppData\Local`), XDG by *purpose*
(config / data / state / cache) — so `%APPDATA%` is not a clean "Windows XDG".

friends to Unix-style `~/.config` / `~/.local/share` paths. XDG-aware tools

#Requires -Version 7
# run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1 — install the toolset with scoop (CLI) +
# winget (GUI). Idempotent: only missing packages are installed. This script is
# the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for what gets installed; re-runs whenever the
# rendered content (i.e. any toggle below) changes.
#
# Toggles (from .chezmoi.toml.tmpl):
#   installCodingAgents  = {{ .installCodingAgents }}
#   installSpecstoryBuild= {{ .installSpecstoryBuild }}
#   installWindowsApps   = {{ .installWindowsApps }}
#   installUtilityApps   = {{ .installUtilityApps }}
#   installGamingApps    = {{ .installGamingApps }}
#   installExtraRuntimes = {{ .installExtraRuntimes }}
#   installMediaTools    = {{ .installMediaTools }}
#   installLlmTools      = {{ .installLlmTools }}
#   installTunnelTools   = {{ .installTunnelTools }}
#   installIacTools      = {{ .installIacTools }}
#   installHerdr         = {{ .installHerdr }}
#   installClink         = {{ .installClink }}
#   installTry           = {{ .installTry }}
#   installTranslate     = {{ .installTranslate }}
#   installInputMethod   = {{ .installInputMethod }}
#   useChineseMirror     = {{ .useChineseMirror }}
#   managedMachine       = {{ .managedMachine }}

# Resilient by design: individual package failures are collected and reported at
# the end, never fatal — one bad manifest must not abort the rest of the install
# (nor the rest of `chezmoi apply`). Mirrors ansible allow-partial-failure.
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
if (Test-Path variable:PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference) { $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $false }
$script:Failures = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()

# UTF-8 console so winget's localized output isn't mojibake on zh-* Windows.
try { [Console]::OutputEncoding = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false) } catch { $null = $_ }
# Package registries: company-approved pull-through feeds on managed machines,
# otherwise optional China/GFW mirrors. Shared with profile.d so apply-time and
# interactive commands cannot drift apart.
{{ template "package-sources.ps1" . }}

function Info($m) { Write-Host "==> $m" -ForegroundColor Cyan }
function Have($n) { [bool](Get-Command $n -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) }
function Register-Failure($what) { $script:Failures.Add($what); Write-Warning "FAILED (skipped): $what" }

# --- scoop -----------------------------------------------------------------
function Test-Admin {
    # $true when this pwsh is running elevated (member of the Administrators role).
    try {
        $id = [Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent()
        ([Security.Principal.WindowsPrincipal]$id).IsInRole([Security.Principal.WindowsBuiltInRole]::Administrator)
    } catch { $false }
}

function Ensure-Scoop {
    if (-not (Have scoop)) {
        # get.scoop.sh returns install.ps1's text. Piping it to Invoke-Expression
        # works in a normal console, but an ELEVATED one is refused ("Running the
        # installer as administrator is disabled by default") unless -RunAsAdmin is
        # passed. Some dev boxes always open the shell as admin, so detect that and
        # forward the flag. We build a scriptblock from the fetched text so we can
        # pass args -- equivalent to `iex "& {$(irm get.scoop.sh)} -RunAsAdmin"`.
        $installer = [scriptblock]::Create((Invoke-RestMethod get.scoop.sh))
        if (Test-Admin) {
            Info 'scoop not found — installing (elevated console: passing -RunAsAdmin)'
            & $installer -RunAsAdmin
        } else {
            Info 'scoop not found — installing (user-scoped, no admin)'
            & $installer
        }
    }
    foreach ($b in 'main', 'extras', 'versions', 'nerd-fonts') {
        scoop bucket add $b *> $null
    }
}

function Get-ScoopInstalled {
    try { return @((scoop export | ConvertFrom-Json).apps.name) } catch { return @() }
}

function Scoop-Install([string[]]$apps) {
    if (-not $apps) { return }
    # Wrap in @() so a lone survivor stays an array. Without it PowerShell
    # unwraps a single match to a bare string, and `scoop install @missing`
    # then splats it one CHARACTER per arg => "Couldn't find manifest for 'm'"
    # when only "mise" was missing.
    $missing = @($apps | Where-Object { ($_ -split '/')[-1] -notin (Get-ScoopInstalled) })
    if (-not $missing) { Info 'scoop: all requested tools already present'; return }
    Info "scoop install: $($missing -join ', ')"
    try { scoop install @missing } catch { Write-Warning "scoop batch error: $_" }
    # Anything still absent after the batch = failed (scoop keeps going past a bad one).
    $after = Get-ScoopInstalled
    foreach ($app in $missing) {
        $name = ($app -split '/')[-1]
        if ($name -notin $after) { Register-Failure "scoop:$name" }
    }
}

# --- winget ----------------------------------------------------------------
function Winget-Install([string]$id) {
    if (-not (Have winget)) { Register-Failure "winget:$id (winget unavailable)"; return }
    winget list --id $id -e --accept-source-agreements *> $null
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) { return }   # already installed
    Info "winget install $id"
    winget install --id $id -e --silent --scope user `
        --accept-source-agreements --accept-package-agreements 2>&1 | Out-Host
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        # some packages don't support --scope user; retry machine scope.
        winget install --id $id -e --silent `
            --accept-source-agreements --accept-package-agreements 2>&1 | Out-Host
    }
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Register-Failure "winget:$id" }
}

# Microsoft Store packages (installed by Store product id via the msstore
# source) — used for apps with no community winget manifest, e.g. Raycast and the
# official ChatGPT desktop app. msstore ignores --scope, so we don't pass it.
function Winget-InstallStore([string]$id) {
    if (-not (Have winget)) { Register-Failure "msstore:$id (winget unavailable)"; return }
    winget list --id $id -e --accept-source-agreements *> $null
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) { return }   # already installed
    Info "winget (msstore) install $id"
    winget install --id $id -e --source msstore --silent `
        --accept-source-agreements --accept-package-agreements 2>&1 | Out-Host
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Register-Failure "msstore:$id" }
}

# --- npm CLI agents --------------------------------------------------------
function Npm-InstallGlobal([string[]]$pkgs) {
    if (-not (Have npm)) { foreach ($p in $pkgs) { Register-Failure "npm:$p (npm unavailable)" }; return }
    foreach ($p in $pkgs) {
        Info "npm i -g $p"
        npm install -g $p 2>&1 | Out-Host
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Register-Failure "npm:$p" }
    }
}

# --- herdr (native Windows terminal multiplexer, preview beta) --------------
# No scoop/winget/npm manifest — installs via herdr.dev's irm|iex bootstrap
# (same shape as Ensure-Scoop). Windows builds are preview-only; the bin junction
# is %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Herdr\bin (added to PATH in profile.d/00_env.ps1).
function Install-Herdr {
    $herdrBin = Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA 'Programs\Herdr\bin\herdr.exe'
    if ((Have herdr) -or (Test-Path -LiteralPath $herdrBin)) { Info 'herdr already installed'; return }
    Info 'installing herdr (preview) via herdr.dev/install.ps1'
    try {
        $env:HERDR_CHANNEL = 'preview'   # Windows builds are preview-only
        $installer = [scriptblock]::Create((Invoke-RestMethod https://herdr.dev/install.ps1))
        & $installer
        if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $herdrBin)) { Register-Failure 'herdr' }
    } catch {
        Write-Warning "herdr install error: $_"
        Register-Failure 'herdr'
    }
}

# herdr-plus — third-party herdr plugin backing the prefix+y (Quick Actions) and
# prefix+O (Projects) keybinds, plus the copy-pane Quick Actions this repo deploys
# to ~/.config/herdr/plugins/config/cloudmanic.herdr-plus/. We ship that CONFIG and
# those KEYBINDS, so not installing the plugin leaves both keys silently dead —
# hence installing it here rather than leaving it to the user.
#
# Requires go: the plugin's Windows build command is `go build -o bin/herdr-plus.exe .`
# (its sh-based build is skipped on Windows). go is gated behind installExtraRuntimes,
# so SKIP with an actionable message rather than failing when it is absent.
# `--yes` accepts the interactive "Install this plugin? [y/N]" prompt. Keep it
# after the repository argument: the Windows preview parses options in that order.
# NB: the keybinds must target the `-windows` action ids — herdr-plus scopes
# `quick-actions`/`projects` to linux+macos. See
# pitfalls/herdr-plus-action-does-not-support-platform-windows.md
function Install-HerdrPlus {
    if (-not (Have herdr)) { return }   # herdr install failed/skipped; nothing to add to
    $installed = $false
    try { $installed = ((herdr plugin list 2>&1) -join "`n") -match 'cloudmanic\.herdr-plus' } catch { $installed = $false }
    if ($installed) { Info 'herdr-plus plugin already installed'; return }
    if (-not (Have go)) {
        Info 'herdr-plus: skipped — needs go to build on Windows (scoop install go, or enable Extra runtimes)'
        return
    }
    Info 'herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus (backs prefix+y / prefix+O)'
    try {
        herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus --yes 2>&1 | Out-Host
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Register-Failure 'herdr-plus' }
    } catch {
        Write-Warning "herdr-plus install error: $_"
        Register-Failure 'herdr-plus'
    }
}

# --- Rime / Weasel (小狼毫) — Traditional Chinese input method ---------------
# Not routed through Winget-Install because two things need overriding:
#
#  1. The manifest is machine-scope NSIS, so `--scope user` can never work and
#     the install always raises UAC (same class as installWsl / installSshServer).
#  2. winget's silent switch for nullsoft is /S, and weasel's install.nsi maps a
#     bare /S to `WeaselSetup.exe /s` = register the TSF service as SIMPLIFIED
#     Chinese. Passing /T as well makes it use /t (Traditional) instead. Silent
#     mode also skips the 安裝選項 dialog and auto-runs WeaselDeployer.exe /deploy.
#
# `winget list` can't be used for the installed check: the manifest's ProductCode
# is "Weasel" but the ARP entry is the localized display name, so we read the
# InstallDir the NSIS installer writes to HKLM instead — which is also how we
# locate WeaselSetup.exe afterwards.
function Install-Weasel {
    $key = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Rime\Weasel'
    $dir = (Get-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name InstallDir -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).InstallDir
    if (-not $dir) {
        if (-not (Have winget)) { Register-Failure 'winget:Rime.Weasel (winget unavailable)'; return }
        Info 'winget install Rime.Weasel (machine scope — expect a UAC prompt)'
        winget install --id Rime.Weasel -e --silent --custom '/T' `
            --accept-source-agreements --accept-package-agreements 2>&1 | Out-Host
        $dir = (Get-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name InstallDir -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).InstallDir
        if (-not $dir) { Register-Failure 'winget:Rime.Weasel'; return }
    } else {
        Info 'Weasel already installed'
    }
    # WeaselSetup's undocumented CLI (WeaselSetup/WeaselSetup.cpp). These two
    # only write HKCU, so they need no elevation and are safe to re-run.
    #   /lt          -> Weasel's own UI in 繁體中文
    #   /toggleascii -> Ctrl+Space toggles ASCII rather than the whole IME,
    #                   which is what makes global_ascii in weasel.custom.yaml
    #                   behave like a single 中/英 switch.
    $setup = Join-Path $dir 'WeaselSetup.exe'
    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $setup) {
        & $setup /lt
        & $setup /toggleascii
    } else {
        Register-Failure 'weasel (WeaselSetup.exe not found; UI language + Ctrl+Space unset)'
    }
}

# ===========================================================================
Ensure-Scoop

# Core CLI toolset — the shell baseline, always installed.
Scoop-Install @(
    'git', 'gh', 'glab', '7zip', 'make', 'just',
    'starship', 'zoxide', 'fzf', 'fd', 'ripgrep', 'bat', 'eza', 'glow', 'jq',
    'delta', 'lazygit', 'neovim', 'yazi', 'btop', 'television', 'tlrc',
    'uv', 'gnupg',
    # Runtimes are NATIVE via scoop, not mise: mise's activate/shims are
    # unreliable on Windows and it has no windows-arm64 bun build. node + bun
    # here; Python via uv (below); go/rust/ruby under Extra runtimes.
    # copilot-proxy needs bun/bunx.
    'nodejs-lts', 'bun',
    # LazyVim pins nvim-treesitter to the `main` branch, which compiles parsers
    # by shelling out to `tree-sitter build`. That CLI compiles via Rust's `cc`
    # crate, which only knows MSVC / GCC / Clang -- NOT zig (only the retired
    # `master` branch accepted zig). So the parser compiler must be a real gcc on
    # PATH; zig here does nothing. scoop's `gcc` is nuwen MinGW-w64, amd64-only --
    # which also matches the amd64 nvim (native on x64, x64-emulated on ARM64), so
    # this ONE line covers both arches (previously gcc was ARM64-only). Plus the
    # tree-sitter CLI `main` requires, and win32yank so `unnamedplus` yanks reach
    # the Windows clipboard. (Leaner gcc alt: scoop `mingw` = niXman MinGW-w64 UCRT.)
    'gcc', 'tree-sitter', 'win32yank'
)

# gh-dash: GitHub PR/issue dashboard TUI (`gh dash`). It's a gh extension, not a
# scoop package, so it needs gh to be authenticated -- this no-ops on a fresh
# machine until `gh auth login`. run_onchange only re-fires when this script
# changes, so after authenticating, install by hand (`gh extension install
# dlvhdr/gh-dash`) or force a reapply (`chezmoi state delete-bucket
# --bucket=entryState`). gh-notify / gh-select from the Unix repo are bash-only
# extensions and are intentionally skipped on Windows.
if (Have gh) {
    gh auth status *> $null
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) {
        $ghExts = gh extension list 2>$null | Out-String
        if ($ghExts -notmatch 'dlvhdr/gh-dash') {
            Info 'gh extension install dlvhdr/gh-dash'
            gh extension install dlvhdr/gh-dash
            if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Register-Failure 'gh-ext:gh-dash' }
        }
    } else {
        Info 'gh not authenticated -- skipping gh-dash (gh auth login, then reapply)'
    }
}

# node/bun come from scoop above (on ~/scoop/shims, reliably on PATH). We do NOT
# use mise here -- see the runtimes note in the core scoop list.

# Default Python, uv-managed. --default also creates unversioned python/python3
# (not just python3.x) in UV_PYTHON_BIN_DIR (~/.local/bin, on PATH via 00_env
# ahead of the Store's python.exe app-alias). On uv 0.8+ `--default` lives behind
# preview mode, so it must be paired with `--preview` (older uv just ignored it) —
# without it, current uv errors: "`--default` is only available in preview mode".
if (Have uv) {
    Info 'uv python install --default --preview'
    $env:UV_PYTHON_BIN_DIR = Join-Path $HOME '.local\bin'
    uv python install --default --preview 2>&1 | Out-Host
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Register-Failure 'uv:python' }
}

# Make PSGallery usable non-interactively before Install-Module (NuGet provider
# + trust) so the fzf key bindings / audio cmdlets install reliably.
try {
    if (-not (Get-PackageProvider -Name NuGet -ListAvailable -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
        Install-PackageProvider -Name NuGet -Scope CurrentUser -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null
    }
    if ((Get-PSRepository -Name PSGallery -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).InstallationPolicy -ne 'Trusted') {
        Set-PSRepository -Name PSGallery -InstallationPolicy Trusted -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    }
} catch { Write-Warning "PSGallery prep failed (non-fatal): $_" }

# PSReadLine ships with pwsh; PSFzf powers the fzf key bindings in profile.d
# (Ctrl+t = files, Ctrl+r = fuzzy history search).
if (-not (Get-Module -ListAvailable -Name PSFzf)) {
    Info 'Install-Module PSFzf'
    Install-Module PSFzf -Scope CurrentUser -Force -AcceptLicense -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
}
# AudioDeviceCmdlets: absolute volume + explicit mute for the sys* helpers.
if (-not (Get-Module -ListAvailable -Name AudioDeviceCmdlets)) {
    Info 'Install-Module AudioDeviceCmdlets'
    Install-Module AudioDeviceCmdlets -Scope CurrentUser -Force -AcceptLicense -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
}

{{ if .installExtraRuntimes -}}
# Extra language runtimes, native via scoop (rust via rustup). node/bun/uv are
# baseline; go/rust/ruby added here.
Scoop-Install @('go', 'rustup', 'ruby')
{{ end -}}

{{ if .installMediaTools -}}
Scoop-Install @('ffmpeg', 'imagemagick')
{{ end -}}

{{ if .installCodingAgents -}}
# AI coding agents. Claude Code ships a native Windows build via winget
# (Anthropic.ClaudeCode — distinct from Anthropic.Claude, the desktop app in the
# GUI block below), so it no longer rides on npm; upgrades come with
# `just upgrade-winget`. The rest are npm-based CLIs; Antigravity IDE is winget.
Winget-Install 'Anthropic.ClaudeCode'
Npm-InstallGlobal @(
    'opencode-ai',
    '@openai/codex',
    '@github/copilot'
)
# NOTE: SpecStory ships no native-Windows CLI (macOS: brew; Linux/WSL: GitHub
# release binaries only), so it is intentionally omitted -- `npm i -g
# @specstory/cli` 404s. The Copilot module already no-ops when `specstory` is
# absent. An experimental Windows build from the unmerged PR #191 is opt-in via
# the installSpecstoryBuild toggle (block below) or `just specstory-build`
# (see backlog/specstory-windows-native-cli.md).

# OpenCode Desktop (GUI companion to the opencode-ai CLI) via scoop extras.
Scoop-Install @('extras/opencode-desktop')

# apprise -> Windows toast notifications for the Claude Code notify hook
# (~/.claude/hooks/notify.ps1, wired via claude/settings-overlay.json). Its
# windows:// backend imports win32api/win32con/win32gui, so pull pywin32 into
# the tool venv (--with). uv tool bin (~/.local/bin) is already on PATH via
# profile.d/00_env.ps1. Mirrors the LiteLLM uv-tool precedent below.
if (Have uv) {
    Info 'uv tool install apprise (+pywin32 for windows://)'
    uv tool install --with pywin32 apprise
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Register-Failure 'uv:apprise' }
}

# peon-ping — game-character voice lines for agent events (CESP player; packs
# from the OpenPeon registry). Installed regardless of the `agentSounds` tier so
# `peon preview` / `peon packs list` are always available to experiment with;
# the tier only decides whether HOOKS get wired, and that happens in
# run_onchange_after_25_claude_settings.ps1.tmpl.
#
# `--openpeon` reroots the whole install at the tool-agnostic ~/.openpeon so the
# installer never touches ~/.claude/settings.json — hook wiring is ours to
# declare (same rule the parent repo applies to workmux's `wm setup`).
# NB: the PowerShell installer's param block is
#   param([string[]]$Packs, [switch]$All, [string]$Lang, [switch]$Local,
#         [switch]$Global, [switch]$OpenPeon, [switch]$InitLocalConfig)
# — there is NO -NoRc (that is the bash install.sh flag only), and it does not
# touch $PROFILE, so nothing extra is needed to keep our profile clean.
# Idempotent: skipped once peon.ps1 exists.
$peonRoot = Join-Path $HOME '.openpeon'
$peonHook = Join-Path $peonRoot 'hooks\peon-ping\peon.ps1'
if (-not (Test-Path $peonHook)) {
    Info 'peon-ping (agent completion sounds, ~/.openpeon root)'
    try {
        # Upstream install.ps1 dot-sources scripts/install-utils.ps1 relative to
        # $PSScriptRoot when run via -File; it only self-downloads that helper
        # when $PSScriptRoot is empty (irm|iex). So stage BOTH files preserving
        # the scripts/ layout in a temp dir, then run install.ps1 with -File.
        $peonStage = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'peon-ping-install'
        New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path (Join-Path $peonStage 'scripts') | Out-Null
        $peonInstaller = Join-Path $peonStage 'install.ps1'
        Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing -ErrorAction Stop `
            -Uri 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PeonPing/peon-ping/main/install.ps1' `
            -OutFile $peonInstaller
        Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing -ErrorAction Stop `
            -Uri 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PeonPing/peon-ping/main/scripts/install-utils.ps1' `
            -OutFile (Join-Path $peonStage 'scripts\install-utils.ps1')
        & powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $peonInstaller `
            -OpenPeon -Packs 'league_of_legends'
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Register-Failure 'peon-ping' }
        # The installer downloads the pack but leaves default_pack="peon" — a pack
        # that ships NO sounds — so a fresh install is silent ("No sound files
        # found for pack 'peon'"). Activate the pack we just seeded. Runs only on
        # first install (whole block is guarded on peon.ps1 absence), so a pack the
        # user later switches to via `peon packs use` is never clobbered.
        $peonCli = Join-Path $HOME '.local\bin\peon.cmd'
        if (Test-Path $peonCli) {
            & $peonCli packs use league_of_legends
            if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Register-Failure 'peon-ping:activate-pack' }
        } else {
            Register-Failure 'peon-ping:activate-pack (peon CLI shim missing)'
        }
    } catch {
        Register-Failure 'peon-ping'
    }
} else {
    Info 'peon-ping already installed — skipping (upgrade: peon update)'
}
{{ end -}}

{{ if .installSpecstoryBuild -}}
# EXPERIMENTAL SpecStory Windows CLI. There is no native-Windows release yet;
# Windows/WSL support lives in the unmerged getspecstory PR #191. Build it from
# source (opt-in) and drop specstory.exe in ~/.local/bin so the Copilot module's
# session auto-save (claude-copilot) can pick it up. Needs git (core) + go (enable
# Extra runtimes, or `scoop install go`). Treat as experimental — may break until
# the PR lands. Tracking + revisit criteria: backlog/specstory-windows-native-cli.md.
if ((Have git) -and (Have go)) {
    try {
        $ssCache = Join-Path $HOME '.cache\specstory-build'
        $ssRepo  = Join-Path $ssCache 'getspecstory'
        $ssBin   = Join-Path $HOME '.local\bin'
        New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $ssCache, $ssBin | Out-Null
        if (-not (Test-Path (Join-Path $ssRepo '.git'))) {
            Info 'specstory: cloning specstoryai/getspecstory'
            git clone --filter=blob:none https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory.git $ssRepo
        }
        Push-Location $ssRepo
        try {
            Info 'specstory: fetching PR #191'
            git fetch origin 'pull/191/head:pr-191' --force
            git checkout --force 'pr-191'
            $ssOut = Join-Path $ssBin 'specstory.exe'
            Push-Location (Join-Path $ssRepo 'specstory-cli')
            try { Info "specstory: go build -> $ssOut"; go build -o $ssOut . } finally { Pop-Location }
            if (Test-Path $ssOut) { Info "specstory: built $ssOut" }
            else { Register-Failure 'specstory-build (go build produced no binary)' }
        } finally { Pop-Location }
    } catch {
        Write-Warning "specstory-build error: $_"
        Register-Failure 'specstory-build'
    }
} else {
    Register-Failure 'specstory-build (needs git + go; enable Extra runtimes or run: scoop install go)'
}
{{ end -}}

{{ if .installClink -}}
# Clink = Bash-style line editing for cmd.exe, so starship / zoxide / fzf work in
# the DOS prompt too (scoop main bucket). pwsh stays the default shell; this is an
# opt-in secondary target with prompt + navigation parity only. Our starship.lua
# deploys via chezmoi (AppData/Local/clink/starship.lua). The zoxide / fzf Clink
# bridges have no scoop/winget manifest (and zoxide has no native cmd target), so
# -- like herdr -- we fetch them from upstream into the Clink profile dir at apply
# time. Network/offline failures are collected, never fatal; starship still works.
Scoop-Install @('clink')
if (Have clink) {
    clink autorun install *> $null                 # HKCU AutoRun; inject into every cmd.exe (no admin)
    $clinkDir = Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA 'clink'
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $clinkDir | Out-Null
    $clinkPlugins = @{
        'zoxide.lua' = 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shunsambongi/clink-zoxide/master/zoxide.lua'
        'fzf.lua'    = 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chrisant996/clink-fzf/master/fzf.lua'
    }
    foreach ($name in $clinkPlugins.Keys) {
        Info "clink plugin: $name"
        try { Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing -Uri $clinkPlugins[$name] -OutFile (Join-Path $clinkDir $name) }
        catch { Register-Failure "clink-plugin:$name" }
    }
    # fzf.default_bindings is a setting DEFINED INSIDE fzf.lua, and `clink set`
    # reloads the profile scripts first -- so this must run AFTER fzf.lua is
    # downloaded above, else the setting is unknown and the value is silently
    # not persisted (the *> $null swallows the "unknown setting" error).
    clink set fzf.default_bindings true *> $null    # Ctrl-R history / Ctrl-T files / Alt-C dir
} else { Register-Failure 'clink (autorun/plugins not configured)' }
{{ end -}}

# be present via installExtraRuntimes; install it regardless so installTry is
# self-contained (Scoop-Install no-ops if ruby is already there). The pwsh
# integration lives in profile.d/32_try.ps1 (command: `tri`).
Scoop-Install @('ruby')
if (Have gem) {
    Info 'gem install try-cli'
{{- if .useChineseMirror }}
    gem install --clear-sources --source https://gems.ruby-china.com try-cli 2>&1 | Out-Host
{{- else }}
    gem install try-cli 2>&1 | Out-Host

} else { Register-Failure 'gem:try-cli (ruby/gem unavailable)' }

{{ if .installTranslate -}}
# translate -- terminal translator CLI+TUI (github.com/daviddwlee84/translate).
# There is no scoop/winget manifest and no prebuilt Windows release, so it is
# built from source with `go install` -- the same path the parent repo takes on
# Linux (dot_ansible/roles/go_tools); macOS there uses the Homebrew tap.
# GOBIN/GOPATH mirror that unix convention: the binary lands in ~/.local/bin
# (already on PATH via profile.d/00_env.ps1) and the module cache in
# ~/.local/share/go rather than recreating ~/go.
#
# It is pure Go (modernc.org/sqlite -- no cgo) and cross-compiles cleanly for
# windows/amd64 and windows/arm64. The FIRST build is slow (several minutes: the
# embedded swagger-ui bundle + sqlite); later applies no-op via the version check
# below. Bump $translateVersion to upgrade -- editing it re-renders this script,
# which is what re-fires the run_onchange. go.mod needs go >= 1.26.4; the default
# GOTOOLCHAIN=auto fetches a newer toolchain if scoop's go is older.
$translateVersion = 'v0.5.2'
Scoop-Install @('go')   # self-contained: installExtraRuntimes may well be off
if (Have go) {
    $trBin  = Join-Path $HOME '.local\bin\translate.exe'
    $trHave = ''
    # `translate --version` prints "translate version v0.5.2 ..."; a module-proxy
    # build carries no VCS metadata, so token 3 is exactly the module version. An
    # absent/unparseable answer just falls through to a reinstall, which is cheap
    # once the module cache is warm.
    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $trBin) {
        try { $trHave = ((& $trBin --version 2>$null) -split '\s+')[2] } catch { $trHave = '' }
    }
    if ($trHave -eq $translateVersion) {
        Info "translate $translateVersion already installed"
    } else {
        Info "go install translate@$translateVersion (first build takes several minutes)"
        $env:GOBIN  = Join-Path $HOME '.local\bin'
        $env:GOPATH = Join-Path $HOME '.local\share\go'
        go install "github.com/daviddwlee84/translate@$translateVersion" 2>&1 | Out-Host
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $trBin)) {
            Register-Failure "go:translate@$translateVersion"
        }
    }
} else {
    Register-Failure 'translate (needs go; enable Extra runtimes or run: scoop install go)'
}
{{ end -}}

Install-Weasel

} else {
    Info 'package install complete — no failures'
}

#Requires -Version 7

BeforeAll {
    $RepoRoot = Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot
    $TemplatePath = Join-Path $RepoRoot '.chezmoitemplates/package-sources.ps1'

    function Render-PackageSources {
        param([bool] $ManagedMachine, [bool] $UseChineseMirror)
        $data = @{
            managedMachine   = $ManagedMachine
            useChineseMirror = $UseChineseMirror
        } | ConvertTo-Json -Compress
        $rendered = & chezmoi execute-template --source $RepoRoot --override-data $data --file $TemplatePath
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'failed to render package-source policy' }
        $rendered -join "`n"
    }
}

Describe 'shared package-source policy' {
    It 'uses company PyPI and npm registries on managed machines' {
        $rendered = Render-PackageSources -ManagedMachine $true -UseChineseMirror $false
        $rendered | Should -Match 'packagefeedproxy\.microsoft\.io/pypi/simple/'
        $rendered | Should -Match 'packagefeedproxy\.microsoft\.io/npm/'
        $rendered | Should -Not -Match 'tuna|npmmirror|goproxy|rsproxy'
    }

    It 'keeps managed-machine policy ahead of China mirrors' {
        $rendered = Render-PackageSources -ManagedMachine $true -UseChineseMirror $true
        $rendered | Should -Match 'packagefeedproxy\.microsoft\.io/pypi/simple/'
        $rendered | Should -Not -Match 'tuna|npmmirror|goproxy|rsproxy'
    }

    It 'uses China mirrors only on an unmanaged opted-in machine' {
        $rendered = Render-PackageSources -ManagedMachine $false -UseChineseMirror $true
        $rendered | Should -Match 'pypi\.tuna\.tsinghua\.edu\.cn'
        $rendered | Should -Match 'registry\.npmmirror\.com'
        $rendered | Should -Match 'goproxy\.cn'
        $rendered | Should -Match 'rsproxy\.cn'
        $rendered | Should -Not -Match 'packagefeedproxy\.microsoft\.io'
    }

    It 'sets no registry overrides by default on an unmanaged machine' {
        $rendered = Render-PackageSources -ManagedMachine $false -UseChineseMirror $false
        $rendered | Should -Not -Match '\$env:(PIP_INDEX_URL|UV_DEFAULT_INDEX|npm_config_registry|GOPROXY)\s*='
    }

    It 'is embedded by install-time, modify-time, and interactive-shell entry points' {
        Get-Content -Raw (Join-Path $RepoRoot '.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1.tmpl') |
            Should -Match 'template "package-sources\.ps1"'
        Get-Content -Raw (Join-Path $RepoRoot 'dot_config/herdr/modify_config.toml.ps1.tmpl') |
            Should -Match 'template "package-sources\.ps1"'
        Get-Content -Raw (Join-Path $RepoRoot 'dot_config/powershell/profile.d/05_mirrors.ps1.tmpl') |
            Should -Match 'template "package-sources\.ps1"'
    }
}

#Requires -Version 7
# run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1 — install the toolset with scoop (CLI) +
# winget (GUI). Idempotent: only missing packages are installed. This script is
# the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for what gets installed; re-runs whenever the
# rendered content (i.e. any toggle below) changes.
#
# Toggles (from .chezmoi.toml.tmpl):
#   installCodingAgents  = {{ .installCodingAgents }}
#   installSpecstoryBuild= {{ .installSpecstoryBuild }}
#   installWindowsApps   = {{ .installWindowsApps }}
#   installUtilityApps   = {{ .installUtilityApps }}
#   installGamingApps    = {{ .installGamingApps }}
#   installExtraRuntimes = {{ .installExtraRuntimes }}
#   installMediaTools    = {{ .installMediaTools }}
#   installLlmTools      = {{ .installLlmTools }}
#   installTunnelTools   = {{ .installTunnelTools }}
#   installIacTools      = {{ .installIacTools }}
#   installHerdr         = {{ .installHerdr }}
#   installClink         = {{ .installClink }}
#   installTry           = {{ .installTry }}
#   installTranslate     = {{ .installTranslate }}
#   installInputMethod   = {{ .installInputMethod }}
#   useChineseMirror     = {{ .useChineseMirror }}
#   managedMachine       = {{ .managedMachine }}

# Resilient by design: individual package failures are collected and reported at
# the end, never fatal — one bad manifest must not abort the rest of the install
# (nor the rest of `chezmoi apply`). Mirrors ansible allow-partial-failure.
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
if (Test-Path variable:PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference) { $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $false }
$script:Failures = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()

# UTF-8 console so winget's localized output isn't mojibake on zh-* Windows.
try { [Console]::OutputEncoding = [System.Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false) } catch { $null = $_ }
# Package registries: company-approved pull-through feeds on managed machines,
# otherwise optional China/GFW mirrors. Shared with profile.d so apply-time and
# interactive commands cannot drift apart.
{{ template "package-sources.ps1" . }}

function Info($m) { Write-Host "==> $m" -ForegroundColor Cyan }
function Have($n) { [bool](Get-Command $n -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) }
function Register-Failure($what) { $script:Failures.Add($what); Write-Warning "FAILED (skipped): $what" }

# --- scoop -----------------------------------------------------------------
function Test-Admin {
    # $true when this pwsh is running elevated (member of the Administrators role).
    try {
        $id = [Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent()
        ([Security.Principal.WindowsPrincipal]$id).IsInRole([Security.Principal.WindowsBuiltInRole]::Administrator)
    } catch { $false }
}

function Ensure-Scoop {
    if (-not (Have scoop)) {
        # get.scoop.sh returns install.ps1's text. Piping it to Invoke-Expression
        # works in a normal console, but an ELEVATED one is refused ("Running the
        # installer as administrator is disabled by default") unless -RunAsAdmin is
        # passed. Some dev boxes always open the shell as admin, so detect that and
        # forward the flag. We build a scriptblock from the fetched text so we can
        # pass args -- equivalent to `iex "& {$(irm get.scoop.sh)} -RunAsAdmin"`.
        $installer = [scriptblock]::Create((Invoke-RestMethod get.scoop.sh))
        if (Test-Admin) {
            Info 'scoop not found — installing (elevated console: passing -RunAsAdmin)'
            & $installer -RunAsAdmin
        } else {
            Info 'scoop not found — installing (user-scoped, no admin)'
            & $installer
        }
    }
    foreach ($b in 'main', 'extras', 'versions', 'nerd-fonts') {
        scoop bucket add $b *> $null
    }
}

function Get-ScoopInstalled {
    try { return @((scoop export | ConvertFrom-Json).apps.name) } catch { return @() }
}

function Scoop-Install([string[]]$apps) {
    if (-not $apps) { return }
    # Wrap in @() so a lone survivor stays an array. Without it PowerShell
    # unwraps a single match to a bare string, and `scoop install @missing`
    # then splats it one CHARACTER per arg => "Couldn't find manifest for 'm'"
    # when only "mise" was missing.
    $missing = @($apps | Where-Object { ($_ -split '/')[-1] -notin (Get-ScoopInstalled) })
    if (-not $missing) { Info 'scoop: all requested tools already present'; return }
    Info "scoop install: $($missing -join ', ')"
    try { scoop install @missing } catch { Write-Warning "scoop batch error: $_" }
    # Anything still absent after the batch = failed (scoop keeps going past a bad one).
    $after = Get-ScoopInstalled
    foreach ($app in $missing) {
        $name = ($app -split '/')[-1]
        if ($name -notin $after) { Register-Failure "scoop:$name" }
    }
}

# --- winget ----------------------------------------------------------------
function Winget-Install([string]$id) {
    if (-not (Have winget)) { Register-Failure "winget:$id (winget unavailable)"; return }
    winget list --id $id -e --accept-source-agreements *> $null
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) { return }   # already installed
    Info "winget install $id"
    winget install --id $id -e --silent --scope user `
        --accept-source-agreements --accept-package-agreements 2>&1 | Out-Host
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        # some packages don't support --scope user; retry machine scope.
        winget install --id $id -e --silent `
            --accept-source-agreements --accept-package-agreements 2>&1 | Out-Host
    }
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Register-Failure "winget:$id" }
}

# Microsoft Store packages (installed by Store product id via the msstore
# source) — used for apps with no community winget manifest, e.g. Raycast and the
# official ChatGPT desktop app. msstore ignores --scope, so we don't pass it.
function Winget-InstallStore([string]$id) {
    if (-not (Have winget)) { Register-Failure "msstore:$id (winget unavailable)"; return }
    winget list --id $id -e --accept-source-agreements *> $null
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) { return }   # already installed
    Info "winget (msstore) install $id"
    winget install --id $id -e --source msstore --silent `
        --accept-source-agreements --accept-package-agreements 2>&1 | Out-Host
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Register-Failure "msstore:$id" }
}

# --- npm CLI agents --------------------------------------------------------
function Npm-InstallGlobal([string[]]$pkgs) {
    if (-not (Have npm)) { foreach ($p in $pkgs) { Register-Failure "npm:$p (npm unavailable)" }; return }
    foreach ($p in $pkgs) {
        Info "npm i -g $p"
        npm install -g $p 2>&1 | Out-Host
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Register-Failure "npm:$p" }
    }
}

# --- herdr (native Windows terminal multiplexer, preview beta) --------------
# No scoop/winget/npm manifest — installs via herdr.dev's irm|iex bootstrap
# (same shape as Ensure-Scoop). Windows builds are preview-only; the bin junction
# is %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Herdr\bin (added to PATH in profile.d/00_env.ps1).
function Install-Herdr {
    $herdrBin = Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA 'Programs\Herdr\bin\herdr.exe'
    if ((Have herdr) -or (Test-Path -LiteralPath $herdrBin)) { Info 'herdr already installed'; return }
    Info 'installing herdr (preview) via herdr.dev/install.ps1'
    try {
        $env:HERDR_CHANNEL = 'preview'   # Windows builds are preview-only
        $installer = [scriptblock]::Create((Invoke-RestMethod https://herdr.dev/install.ps1))
        & $installer
        if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $herdrBin)) { Register-Failure 'herdr' }
    } catch {
        Write-Warning "herdr install error: $_"
        Register-Failure 'herdr'
    }
}

# herdr-plus — third-party herdr plugin backing the prefix+y (Quick Actions) and
# prefix+O (Projects) keybinds, plus the copy-pane Quick Actions this repo deploys
# to ~/.config/herdr/plugins/config/cloudmanic.herdr-plus/. We ship that CONFIG and
# those KEYBINDS, so not installing the plugin leaves both keys silently dead —
# hence installing it here rather than leaving it to the user.
#
# Requires go: the plugin's Windows build command is `go build -o bin/herdr-plus.exe .`
# (its sh-based build is skipped on Windows). go is gated behind installExtraRuntimes,
# so SKIP with an actionable message rather than failing when it is absent.
# `--yes` accepts the interactive "Install this plugin? [y/N]" prompt. Keep it
# after the repository argument: the Windows preview parses options in that order.
# NB: the keybinds must target the `-windows` action ids — herdr-plus scopes
# `quick-actions`/`projects` to linux+macos. See
# pitfalls/herdr-plus-action-does-not-support-platform-windows.md
function Install-HerdrPlus {
    if (-not (Have herdr)) { return }   # herdr install failed/skipped; nothing to add to
    $installed = $false
    try { $installed = ((herdr plugin list 2>&1) -join "`n") -match 'cloudmanic\.herdr-plus' } catch { $installed = $false }
    if ($installed) { Info 'herdr-plus plugin already installed'; return }
    if (-not (Have go)) {
        Info 'herdr-plus: skipped — needs go to build on Windows (scoop install go, or enable Extra runtimes)'
        return
    }
    Info 'herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus (backs prefix+y / prefix+O)'
    try {
        herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus --yes 2>&1 | Out-Host
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Register-Failure 'herdr-plus' }
    } catch {
        Write-Warning "herdr-plus install error: $_"
        Register-Failure 'herdr-plus'
    }
}

# --- Rime / Weasel (小狼毫) — Traditional Chinese input method ---------------
# Not routed through Winget-Install because two things need overriding:
#
#  1. The manifest is machine-scope NSIS, so `--scope user` can never work and
#     the install always raises UAC (same class as installWsl / installSshServer).
#  2. winget's silent switch for nullsoft is /S, and weasel's install.nsi maps a
#     bare /S to `WeaselSetup.exe /s` = register the TSF service as SIMPLIFIED
#     Chinese. Passing /T as well makes it use /t (Traditional) instead. Silent
#     mode also skips the 安裝選項 dialog and auto-runs WeaselDeployer.exe /deploy.
#
# `winget list` can't be used for the installed check: the manifest's ProductCode
# is "Weasel" but the ARP entry is the localized display name, so we read the
# InstallDir the NSIS installer writes to HKLM instead — which is also how we
# locate WeaselSetup.exe afterwards.
function Install-Weasel {
    $key = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Rime\Weasel'
    $dir = (Get-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name InstallDir -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).InstallDir
    if (-not $dir) {
        if (-not (Have winget)) { Register-Failure 'winget:Rime.Weasel (winget unavailable)'; return }
        Info 'winget install Rime.Weasel (machine scope — expect a UAC prompt)'
        winget install --id Rime.Weasel -e --silent --custom '/T' `
            --accept-source-agreements --accept-package-agreements 2>&1 | Out-Host
        $dir = (Get-ItemProperty -Path $key -Name InstallDir -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).InstallDir
        if (-not $dir) { Register-Failure 'winget:Rime.Weasel'; return }
    } else {
        Info 'Weasel already installed'
    }
    # WeaselSetup's undocumented CLI (WeaselSetup/WeaselSetup.cpp). These two
    # only write HKCU, so they need no elevation and are safe to re-run.
    #   /lt          -> Weasel's own UI in 繁體中文
    #   /toggleascii -> Ctrl+Space toggles ASCII rather than the whole IME,
    #                   which is what makes global_ascii in weasel.custom.yaml
    #                   behave like a single 中/英 switch.
    $setup = Join-Path $dir 'WeaselSetup.exe'
    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $setup) {
        & $setup /lt
        & $setup /toggleascii
    } else {
        Register-Failure 'weasel (WeaselSetup.exe not found; UI language + Ctrl+Space unset)'
    }
}

# ===========================================================================
Ensure-Scoop

# Core CLI toolset — the shell baseline, always installed.
Scoop-Install @(
    'git', 'gh', 'glab', '7zip', 'make', 'just',
    'starship', 'zoxide', 'fzf', 'fd', 'ripgrep', 'bat', 'eza', 'glow', 'jq',
    'delta', 'lazygit', 'neovim', 'yazi', 'btop', 'television', 'tlrc',
    'uv', 'gnupg',
    # Runtimes are NATIVE via scoop, not mise: mise's activate/shims are
    # unreliable on Windows and it has no windows-arm64 bun build. node + bun
    # here; Python via uv (below); go/rust/ruby under Extra runtimes.
    # copilot-proxy needs bun/bunx.
    'nodejs-lts', 'bun',
    # LazyVim pins nvim-treesitter to the `main` branch, which compiles parsers
    # by shelling out to `tree-sitter build`. That CLI compiles via Rust's `cc`
    # crate, which only knows MSVC / GCC / Clang -- NOT zig (only the retired
    # `master` branch accepted zig). So the parser compiler must be a real gcc on
    # PATH; zig here does nothing. scoop's `gcc` is nuwen MinGW-w64, amd64-only --
    # which also matches the amd64 nvim (native on x64, x64-emulated on ARM64), so
    # this ONE line covers both arches (previously gcc was ARM64-only). Plus the
    # tree-sitter CLI `main` requires, and win32yank so `unnamedplus` yanks reach
    # the Windows clipboard. (Leaner gcc alt: scoop `mingw` = niXman MinGW-w64 UCRT.)
    'gcc', 'tree-sitter', 'win32yank'
)

# gh-dash: GitHub PR/issue dashboard TUI (`gh dash`). It's a gh extension, not a
# scoop package, so it needs gh to be authenticated -- this no-ops on a fresh
# machine until `gh auth login`. run_onchange only re-fires when this script
# changes, so after authenticating, install by hand (`gh extension install
# dlvhdr/gh-dash`) or force a reapply (`chezmoi state delete-bucket
# --bucket=entryState`). gh-notify / gh-select from the Unix repo are bash-only
# extensions and are intentionally skipped on Windows.
if (Have gh) {
    gh auth status *> $null
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) {
        $ghExts = gh extension list 2>$null | Out-String
        if ($ghExts -notmatch 'dlvhdr/gh-dash') {
            Info 'gh extension install dlvhdr/gh-dash'
            gh extension install dlvhdr/gh-dash
            if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Register-Failure 'gh-ext:gh-dash' }
        }
    } else {
        Info 'gh not authenticated -- skipping gh-dash (gh auth login, then reapply)'
    }
}

# node/bun come from scoop above (on ~/scoop/shims, reliably on PATH). We do NOT
# use mise here -- see the runtimes note in the core scoop list.

# Default Python, uv-managed. --default also creates unversioned python/python3
# (not just python3.x) in UV_PYTHON_BIN_DIR (~/.local/bin, on PATH via 00_env
# ahead of the Store's python.exe app-alias). On uv 0.8+ `--default` lives behind
# preview mode, so it must be paired with `--preview` (older uv just ignored it) —
# without it, current uv errors: "`--default` is only available in preview mode".
if (Have uv) {
    Info 'uv python install --default --preview'
    $env:UV_PYTHON_BIN_DIR = Join-Path $HOME '.local\bin'
    uv python install --default --preview 2>&1 | Out-Host
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Register-Failure 'uv:python' }
}

# Make PSGallery usable non-interactively before Install-Module (NuGet provider
# + trust) so the fzf key bindings / audio cmdlets install reliably.
try {
    if (-not (Get-PackageProvider -Name NuGet -ListAvailable -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) {
        Install-PackageProvider -Name NuGet -Scope CurrentUser -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null
    }
    if ((Get-PSRepository -Name PSGallery -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).InstallationPolicy -ne 'Trusted') {
        Set-PSRepository -Name PSGallery -InstallationPolicy Trusted -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    }
} catch { Write-Warning "PSGallery prep failed (non-fatal): $_" }

# PSReadLine ships with pwsh; PSFzf powers the fzf key bindings in profile.d
# (Ctrl+t = files, Ctrl+r = fuzzy history search).
if (-not (Get-Module -ListAvailable -Name PSFzf)) {
    Info 'Install-Module PSFzf'
    Install-Module PSFzf -Scope CurrentUser -Force -AcceptLicense -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
}
# AudioDeviceCmdlets: absolute volume + explicit mute for the sys* helpers.
if (-not (Get-Module -ListAvailable -Name AudioDeviceCmdlets)) {
    Info 'Install-Module AudioDeviceCmdlets'
    Install-Module AudioDeviceCmdlets -Scope CurrentUser -Force -AcceptLicense -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
}

{{ if .installExtraRuntimes -}}
# Extra language runtimes, native via scoop (rust via rustup). node/bun/uv are
# baseline; go/rust/ruby added here.
Scoop-Install @('go', 'rustup', 'ruby')
{{ end -}}

{{ if .installMediaTools -}}
Scoop-Install @('ffmpeg', 'imagemagick')
{{ end -}}

{{ if .installCodingAgents -}}
# AI coding agents. Claude Code ships a native Windows build via winget
# (Anthropic.ClaudeCode — distinct from Anthropic.Claude, the desktop app in the
# GUI block below), so it no longer rides on npm; upgrades come with
# `just upgrade-winget`. The rest are npm-based CLIs; Antigravity IDE is winget.
Winget-Install 'Anthropic.ClaudeCode'
Npm-InstallGlobal @(
    'opencode-ai',
    '@openai/codex',
    '@github/copilot'
)
# NOTE: SpecStory ships no native-Windows CLI (macOS: brew; Linux/WSL: GitHub
# release binaries only), so it is intentionally omitted -- `npm i -g
# @specstory/cli` 404s. The Copilot module already no-ops when `specstory` is
# absent. An experimental Windows build from the unmerged PR #191 is opt-in via
# the installSpecstoryBuild toggle (block below) or `just specstory-build`
# (see backlog/specstory-windows-native-cli.md).

# OpenCode Desktop (GUI companion to the opencode-ai CLI) via scoop extras.
Scoop-Install @('extras/opencode-desktop')

# apprise -> Windows toast notifications for the Claude Code notify hook
# (~/.claude/hooks/notify.ps1, wired via claude/settings-overlay.json). Its
# windows:// backend imports win32api/win32con/win32gui, so pull pywin32 into
# the tool venv (--with). uv tool bin (~/.local/bin) is already on PATH via
# profile.d/00_env.ps1. Mirrors the LiteLLM uv-tool precedent below.
if (Have uv) {
    Info 'uv tool install apprise (+pywin32 for windows://)'
    uv tool install --with pywin32 apprise
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Register-Failure 'uv:apprise' }
}

# peon-ping — game-character voice lines for agent events (CESP player; packs
# from the OpenPeon registry). Installed regardless of the `agentSounds` tier so
# `peon preview` / `peon packs list` are always available to experiment with;
# the tier only decides whether HOOKS get wired, and that happens in
# run_onchange_after_25_claude_settings.ps1.tmpl.
#
# `--openpeon` reroots the whole install at the tool-agnostic ~/.openpeon so the
# installer never touches ~/.claude/settings.json — hook wiring is ours to
# declare (same rule the parent repo applies to workmux's `wm setup`).
# NB: the PowerShell installer's param block is
#   param([string[]]$Packs, [switch]$All, [string]$Lang, [switch]$Local,
#         [switch]$Global, [switch]$OpenPeon, [switch]$InitLocalConfig)
# — there is NO -NoRc (that is the bash install.sh flag only), and it does not
# touch $PROFILE, so nothing extra is needed to keep our profile clean.
# Idempotent: skipped once peon.ps1 exists.
$peonRoot = Join-Path $HOME '.openpeon'
$peonHook = Join-Path $peonRoot 'hooks\peon-ping\peon.ps1'
if (-not (Test-Path $peonHook)) {
    Info 'peon-ping (agent completion sounds, ~/.openpeon root)'
    try {
        # Upstream install.ps1 dot-sources scripts/install-utils.ps1 relative to
        # $PSScriptRoot when run via -File; it only self-downloads that helper
        # when $PSScriptRoot is empty (irm|iex). So stage BOTH files preserving
        # the scripts/ layout in a temp dir, then run install.ps1 with -File.
        $peonStage = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'peon-ping-install'
        New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path (Join-Path $peonStage 'scripts') | Out-Null
        $peonInstaller = Join-Path $peonStage 'install.ps1'
        Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing -ErrorAction Stop `
            -Uri 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PeonPing/peon-ping/main/install.ps1' `
            -OutFile $peonInstaller
        Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing -ErrorAction Stop `
            -Uri 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PeonPing/peon-ping/main/scripts/install-utils.ps1' `
            -OutFile (Join-Path $peonStage 'scripts\install-utils.ps1')
        & powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $peonInstaller `
            -OpenPeon -Packs 'league_of_legends'
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Register-Failure 'peon-ping' }
        # The installer downloads the pack but leaves default_pack="peon" — a pack
        # that ships NO sounds — so a fresh install is silent ("No sound files
        # found for pack 'peon'"). Activate the pack we just seeded. Runs only on
        # first install (whole block is guarded on peon.ps1 absence), so a pack the
        # user later switches to via `peon packs use` is never clobbered.
        $peonCli = Join-Path $HOME '.local\bin\peon.cmd'
        if (Test-Path $peonCli) {
            & $peonCli packs use league_of_legends
            if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Register-Failure 'peon-ping:activate-pack' }
        } else {
            Register-Failure 'peon-ping:activate-pack (peon CLI shim missing)'
        }
    } catch {
        Register-Failure 'peon-ping'
    }
} else {
    Info 'peon-ping already installed — skipping (upgrade: peon update)'
}
{{ end -}}

{{ if .installSpecstoryBuild -}}
# EXPERIMENTAL SpecStory Windows CLI. There is no native-Windows release yet;
# Windows/WSL support lives in the unmerged getspecstory PR #191. Build it from
# source (opt-in) and drop specstory.exe in ~/.local/bin so the Copilot module's
# session auto-save (claude-copilot) can pick it up. Needs git (core) + go (enable
# Extra runtimes, or `scoop install go`). Treat as experimental — may break until
# the PR lands. Tracking + revisit criteria: backlog/specstory-windows-native-cli.md.
if ((Have git) -and (Have go)) {
    try {
        $ssCache = Join-Path $HOME '.cache\specstory-build'
        $ssRepo  = Join-Path $ssCache 'getspecstory'
        $ssBin   = Join-Path $HOME '.local\bin'
        New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $ssCache, $ssBin | Out-Null
        if (-not (Test-Path (Join-Path $ssRepo '.git'))) {
            Info 'specstory: cloning specstoryai/getspecstory'
            git clone --filter=blob:none https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory.git $ssRepo
        }
        Push-Location $ssRepo
        try {
            Info 'specstory: fetching PR #191'
            git fetch origin 'pull/191/head:pr-191' --force
            git checkout --force 'pr-191'
            $ssOut = Join-Path $ssBin 'specstory.exe'
            Push-Location (Join-Path $ssRepo 'specstory-cli')
            try { Info "specstory: go build -> $ssOut"; go build -o $ssOut . } finally { Pop-Location }
            if (Test-Path $ssOut) { Info "specstory: built $ssOut" }
            else { Register-Failure 'specstory-build (go build produced no binary)' }
        } finally { Pop-Location }
    } catch {
        Write-Warning "specstory-build error: $_"
        Register-Failure 'specstory-build'
    }
} else {
    Register-Failure 'specstory-build (needs git + go; enable Extra runtimes or run: scoop install go)'
}
{{ end -}}

{{ if .installClink -}}
# Clink = Bash-style line editing for cmd.exe, so starship / zoxide / fzf work in
# the DOS prompt too (scoop main bucket). pwsh stays the default shell; this is an
# opt-in secondary target with prompt + navigation parity only. Our starship.lua
# deploys via chezmoi (AppData/Local/clink/starship.lua). The zoxide / fzf Clink
# bridges have no scoop/winget manifest (and zoxide has no native cmd target), so
# -- like herdr -- we fetch them from upstream into the Clink profile dir at apply
# time. Network/offline failures are collected, never fatal; starship still works.
Scoop-Install @('clink')
if (Have clink) {
    clink autorun install *> $null                 # HKCU AutoRun; inject into every cmd.exe (no admin)
    $clinkDir = Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA 'clink'
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $clinkDir | Out-Null
    $clinkPlugins = @{
        'zoxide.lua' = 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shunsambongi/clink-zoxide/master/zoxide.lua'
        'fzf.lua'    = 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chrisant996/clink-fzf/master/fzf.lua'
    }
    foreach ($name in $clinkPlugins.Keys) {
        Info "clink plugin: $name"
        try { Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing -Uri $clinkPlugins[$name] -OutFile (Join-Path $clinkDir $name) }
        catch { Register-Failure "clink-plugin:$name" }
    }
    # fzf.default_bindings is a setting DEFINED INSIDE fzf.lua, and `clink set`
    # reloads the profile scripts first -- so this must run AFTER fzf.lua is
    # downloaded above, else the setting is unknown and the value is silently
    # not persisted (the *> $null swallows the "unknown setting" error).
    clink set fzf.default_bindings true *> $null    # Ctrl-R history / Ctrl-T files / Alt-C dir
} else { Register-Failure 'clink (autorun/plugins not configured)' }
{{ end -}}

{{ if .installTry -}}
# try (tobi/try) — Ruby ephemeral-workspace CLI (gem try-cli). Ruby may already
# be present via installExtraRuntimes; install it regardless so installTry is
# self-contained (Scoop-Install no-ops if ruby is already there). The pwsh
# integration lives in profile.d/32_try.ps1 (command: `tri`).
Scoop-Install @('ruby')
if (Have gem) {
    Info 'gem install try-cli'
{{- if .useChineseMirror }}
    gem install --clear-sources --source https://gems.ruby-china.com try-cli 2>&1 | Out-Host
{{- else }}
    gem install try-cli 2>&1 | Out-Host
{{- end }}
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Register-Failure 'gem:try-cli' }
} else { Register-Failure 'gem:try-cli (ruby/gem unavailable)' }
{{ end -}}

{{ if .installTranslate -}}
# translate -- terminal translator CLI+TUI (github.com/daviddwlee84/translate).
# There is no scoop/winget manifest and no prebuilt Windows release, so it is
# built from source with `go install` -- the same path the parent repo takes on
# Linux (dot_ansible/roles/go_tools); macOS there uses the Homebrew tap.
# GOBIN/GOPATH mirror that unix convention: the binary lands in ~/.local/bin
# (already on PATH via profile.d/00_env.ps1) and the module cache in
# ~/.local/share/go rather than recreating ~/go.
#
# It is pure Go (modernc.org/sqlite -- no cgo) and cross-compiles cleanly for
# windows/amd64 and windows/arm64. The FIRST build is slow (several minutes: the
# embedded swagger-ui bundle + sqlite); later applies no-op via the version check
# below. Bump $translateVersion to upgrade -- editing it re-renders this script,
# which is what re-fires the run_onchange. go.mod needs go >= 1.26.4; the default
# GOTOOLCHAIN=auto fetches a newer toolchain if scoop's go is older.
$translateVersion = 'v0.5.2'
Scoop-Install @('go')   # self-contained: installExtraRuntimes may well be off
if (Have go) {
    $trBin  = Join-Path $HOME '.local\bin\translate.exe'
    $trHave = ''
    # `translate --version` prints "translate version v0.5.2 ..."; a module-proxy
    # build carries no VCS metadata, so token 3 is exactly the module version. An
    # absent/unparseable answer just falls through to a reinstall, which is cheap
    # once the module cache is warm.
    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $trBin) {
        try { $trHave = ((& $trBin --version 2>$null) -split '\s+')[2] } catch { $trHave = '' }
    }
    if ($trHave -eq $translateVersion) {
        Info "translate $translateVersion already installed"
    } else {
        Info "go install translate@$translateVersion (first build takes several minutes)"
        $env:GOBIN  = Join-Path $HOME '.local\bin'
        $env:GOPATH = Join-Path $HOME '.local\share\go'
        go install "github.com/daviddwlee84/translate@$translateVersion" 2>&1 | Out-Host
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $trBin)) {
            Register-Failure "go:translate@$translateVersion"
        }
    }
} else {
    Register-Failure 'translate (needs go; enable Extra runtimes or run: scoop install go)'
}
{{ end -}}

Install-Weasel
{{ end -}}

} else {
    Info 'package install complete — no failures'
}
